rules.title: Reference to a ref-typed parameter carries that parameter as provenance source
rules.statement: A `VarRef` to a parameter `p` whose type is a reference has provenance source {p}. An `AddrOf p` of a reference parameter likewise yields source {p}. Provenance source identifies which named inputs a returned borrow may point into.

rules.title: Borrow of a local variable is local provenance
rules.statement: `&x` (AddrOf) where x is a tracked local (not a parameter, not a materialized temp) has provenance is_local=true. Such a borrow is valid in scope but dangles if it escapes (e.g. is returned).

rules.title: Borrow of a materialized statement-temporary is statement-scoped (is_temp)
rules.statement: A borrow whose root is a materialized statement-temporary (`__rtmp_N`, the hoisted local for a fresh rvalue receiver in `make().view()` => `(&__rtmp_0).view()`) has provenance is_temp=true: the temporary drops at end of statement, so any reference into it dangles once it escapes the statement.

rules.title: Direct &<temporary> bound to a let is lifetime-extended (local, not statement-temp)
rules.statement: A DIRECT borrow of a literal/struct-literal/call rvalue (`let r = &mut 5;`) is lifetime-extended: the temporary lives as long as the binding, so provenance is is_local (NOT is_temp). It is therefore caught only when returned past the scope, not at the binding site.
rules.uncertainty: Distinction between materialized __rtmp temp (statement-scoped) and direct &temp (lifetime-extended) inferred from the two AddrOfTemp branches.

rules.title: Borrow rooted at a value local is local provenance
rules.statement: A borrow rooted at a by-value local through field/index/deref chains (`&c.x`, `&c.a[i]`, `&*h` where h is a value-local smart pointer) has provenance is_local=true and dangles if returned.

rules.title: Unresolvable borrow provenance is conservatively accepted
rules.statement: When a borrow's root cannot be traced to a parameter, local, or temporary, provenance is empty (unknown) and the borrow is conservatively accepted (treated as caller-owned / non-escaping).

rules.title: Place projections forward the receiver's provenance
rules.statement: Field read, deref, tuple index, cast, and index read forward the provenance of their operand/receiver unchanged.

rules.title: Provenance of a value-producing control-flow expression is the merge of its branches
rules.statement: An if-expr's provenance is the merge of its then and else value provenances; a block-expr's is its result's; a match-expr's is the merge over all arm values. Merge unions param sources and ORs the is_local/is_temp flags.

rules.title: A reference-returning method result borrows its receiver (lifetime elision)
rules.statement: For a method call whose result type is a reference (or a #[borrow_carrying] value type), the result's provenance equals the receiver's provenance (output lifetime ties to &self). A non-ref, non-borrow-carrying result has empty provenance (owned).

rules.title: A ref-self method on a temporary receiver yields a statement-temp borrow
rules.statement: When a ref-self method (self by reference, method_self_kind != 0) is called on a temporary receiver, the result points into that temporary, so provenance is_temp=true. A by-value-self adapter (self: Self) instead consumes/moves the temporary into the result and does not produce a statement-temp escape.

rules.title: Reference result of a method on a bare value-local receiver is local provenance
rules.statement: If a method's reference/borrow-carrying result has otherwise-empty provenance but its receiver roots at a value-local (e.g. `Rc::deref` on `h` directly), the result provenance is marked is_local.

rules.title: A borrow-carrying function result may alias its reference arguments
rules.statement: A free-function/constructor call returning a #[borrow_carrying] value has provenance equal to the merge of the provenances of its reference-typed arguments (`WAny::from(&x)` aliases x). A non-borrow-carrying call result is caller-owned (empty provenance). Value (non-ref) arguments contribute no provenance.

rules.title: Aggregate literal provenance is the merge of its element/field initializers
rules.statement: A struct literal, tuple literal, or enum-data literal has provenance equal to the merge of the provenances of its field values / elements / payloads; returning the aggregate escapes any borrow carried by a borrow-carrying field. Pod/owned fields contribute empty provenance.

rules.title: Returning a reference with local or temporary provenance is rejected as dangling
rules.statement: If the function returns a reference (or borrow-carrying) type and the returned expression's provenance is is_local or is_temp, the return is an error: a reference to a temporary (is_temp / AddrOfTemp source) reports 'cannot return reference to temporary value: dangling reference'; a reference to a named local reports 'cannot return reference to local variable <name>: dangling reference'.

rules.title: Returned borrow source lifetime must equal or outlive the declared return lifetime
rules.statement: When the return type has an explicit (non-'_) lifetime 'ret, each traced parameter source's declared lifetime 'src must satisfy 'src == 'ret OR 'src outlives 'ret (an explicit `where 'src: 'ret`, or 'static); otherwise a 'lifetime mismatch: return type has lifetime 'ret but <src> has lifetime 'src' error is reported.

rules.title: Returns sourced from a non-reference (aggregate) parameter defer to the type checker
rules.statement: When the return-type lifetime check finds no ref-typed parameter sources (provenance traces to a struct/aggregate parameter holding refs, e.g. returning `x.y` with `y: &'b u8`), no lifetime error is raised; the declared-return type match is trusted as already verified by the type checker. Likewise an elided outer ref lifetime over an aggregate-pointing param defers to the type checker.
rules.uncertainty: B86: deferral characterized as compensating for incomplete impl-level lt_arg propagation; the normative content is that such returns are accepted.

rules.title: Elided return lifetime with one reference parameter must derive from that parameter
rules.statement:
When the return lifetime is elided ('_) and exactly one reference-typed parameter exists, the returned reference's provenance must include that sole parameter; otherwise 'lifetime elision: return reference must derive from

(the only reference parameter)' is reported. With multiple ref parameters the source is ambiguous and any param source is accepted.

rules.title: A returned borrow with empty, non-local provenance is accepted
rules.statement: If the returned expression has empty provenance and is not local/temp (e.g. a function-call result, global, or untraceable expression), the return is accepted even when ref parameters exist (conservative non-error).

rules.title: A conditionally-formed reference borrows every branch operand for the holder's scope
rules.statement: When a reference is formed through a control-flow expression (`if c { &mut x } else { &mut y }`, `match t { A => &x, _ => &y }`), a scoped borrow is taken on every branch's borrowed place (both x and y), held under the binding holder. Non-borrow sub-expressions (condition, scrutinee, guards) are visited normally.

rules.title: &place takes a borrow of that place, of the reference's mutability
rules.statement: An `&x` / `&mut x` (AddrOf) takes a scoped borrow of x whose mutability is that of the formed reference type, held under the binding holder.

rules.title: A reborrow registers a borrow on the reference variable, not its pointee
rules.statement: A reborrow of shape `&*r` / `&mut *r` where r is reference-typed registers a borrow on r itself (freezing r for the borrow's scope), not on r's pointee. NLL releases on the holder's last use, restoring r. Reborrow mutability comes from the formed reference, drawing on r's borrow capacity rather than r's binding-mutness.

rules.title: &v[i] borrows the whole indexed container (its receiver)
rules.statement: An indexing reference `&v[i]` / `&mut v[i]` desugars to `&*(Vec::index(&v,i))`; the borrow is recorded on the index method's receiver (the whole container v), so a `v.push()` while the element ref is live is rejected (iterator/element invalidation). `&mut v[i]` forces the receiver borrow to be mutable even when the desugared index_mut self-kind is unresolved.
rules.divergence: Element borrow is whole-container coarse (rustc E0499 parity for aliasing two `&mut v[i]`).

rules.title: A field-path borrow is path-precise; disjoint sibling fields may be borrowed independently
rules.statement: A borrow of a field chain `&o.f.g` takes a path-aware (dotted) borrow on the root, so disjoint sibling fields borrow without conflict; a borrow whose path overlaps (equal or prefix of) a moved field reports 'use of moved field <root>.<f> (moved on line N)'.

rules.title: A field borrow on a union root is a whole-value borrow
rules.statement: When the borrowed place's root is a union, a field-path borrow is redirected to a whole-value borrow of the root (all sibling fields of a union alias).

rules.title: Index/sub-expressions of a borrowed place are checked before the place is borrowed
rules.statement: When a borrowed place contains an index or other sub-expression, the inner expression is visited (its sub-checks run) before the borrow is registered on the root, avoiding a spurious self-conflict where the recursive visit of the root sees its own freshly-set borrow.

rules.title: A call result bound to a reference holds borrows of every reference argument
rules.statement: When a function-call result is bound to a reference (`let r = f(&a, &b)`), each reference-typed argument is borrowed under the holder (the let binding); a mutation or `&mut` of any such argument while r is live is rejected. NLL releases at the holder's last use. (Conservative upper bound matching Rust elision.)

rules.title: A reference-returning method holds a borrow of its receiver for the result's lifetime
rules.statement: A method whose result borrows self (fully-elided &self->&ret, or borrow-carrying result) holds a scoped borrow of the receiver's root place under the holder, with the receiver's mutability; `let v = c.get_ref(); c.set(...)` while v is live is rejected. The borrow is field-precise when the receiver is a field chain, and whole-root otherwise.

rules.title: The receiver borrow mutability follows the method's self kind
rules.statement: The receiver borrow held for a self-borrowing method result is mutable iff the method takes self by mutable reference (method_self_kind == 2) or an outer `&mut` reborrow forced it mutable; otherwise it is shared.

rules.title: Borrows through a raw-pointer root are not tracked
rules.statement: When a self-borrowing method's receiver roots at a raw pointer, no receiver borrow is recorded (raw pointers are outside borrow checking, Rust parity). Borrows through `&`/`&mut` reference roots are tracked.

rules.title: Self-borrowing method results on Rc/Arc roots do not hold a receiver borrow
rules.statement: When a self-borrowing method's bare-VarRef receiver roots at an Rc or Arc value, no scoped receiver borrow is recorded: shared-ownership handles are the blessed interior-mutability domain, so `h.array()` followed by `hold(&mut h, root)` is permitted.
rules.divergence: Logos-specific exemption for Rc/Arc receivers (residency-escape / interior-mutability pattern).
